South Africa · Contact

Request a proposal for a survey in South Africa

A short note is enough: leave your name and email, and a few words about the servitude, reserve or site if you like. We’ll get back to you with the questions we need answered, and then with a written proposal covering the scope, imagery plan, method, deliverables and schedule.

Only your name and email are needed. Everything else is optional.

Your request reaches us through FormSubmit, a form-delivery service. Read the privacy notice.

What happens next

  1. We get back to you by email, or by phone if you left a number.
  2. A short call about the route or site, the distances that matter and the imagery.
  3. A written proposal: scope, imagery plan, method, deliverables and schedule.

No need to prepare anything

A short note is enough. If you have a route or boundary file (KML, KMZ, GeoJSON, Shapefile, GPX or GeoPackage), keep it to hand: we’ll ask for it when we get back to you. No file yet? We can draw the route with you.

Procurement teams

Mention the tender or the supplier portal in your message, and we’ll ask for the documents when we get back to you. The proposal states which registrations are in place for your contract and which are being arranged.

For a servitude or site in South Africa

None of this is needed to get in touch: it is what we’ll ask about when we get back to you.

  • Province and municipality, so we can check the imagery that exists for the area.
  • The widths to report: those in your servitude agreements and diagrams, a building line or company standard, or the SANRAL building restriction area. Up to six widths in one survey.
  • Your own imagery: whether your teams already fly drones along the route, and the dates of the latest orthophotos.
  • Satellite only, or drone detail too. Drone work needs a UASOC operator, an Air Service Licence and landowner permission for each flight, so the proposal shows the lead time. See drone law in South Africa.
  • What the register is for: maintenance and planning, a wayleave, a route baseline, or a record that may be used as evidence, which raises POPIA questions to settle first (POPIA and aerial imagery).

Frequently asked questions

Do you need a site visit or a drone flight to start?

No. A survey starts from your route or boundary file and dated satellite imagery, open building datasets or the orthophotos you already hold, so nobody travels and no aircraft flies. Drone detail is added only where a stretch needs it, subject to the SACAA approvals and landowner permissions each flight requires.

Can we send our own drone orthophotos?

Yes. Tell us roughly how many kilometres or hectares they cover, the capture dates and the format, and we check a sample before we commit. Large files are transferred by a link you choose or one we send; the form on this page is for your request, not for imagery.

We have no route file yet. Can we still ask?

Yes. Describe the line or pipeline, the province and the municipality, or send tower, valve or kilometre-post coordinates, and we draw the route with you and send it back for your confirmation before any survey runs.

Our procurement runs through a portal. Can you respond there?

Yes. Mention the portal and the tender or RFQ number in your message, and when we get back to you we’ll ask for any vendor-registration or POPIA operator forms your organisation uses. Our procurement notes set out what applies to this kind of service.
